While I recognize that the process of righting our national budget will come with growing pains, we must remember Thomas Jefferson's warning that "public debt [is] the greatest of the dangers to be feared." <br /> <br /> If we wish to survive as a nation and preserve the Republic for our children and grandchildren, Congress must stop spending money we do not have and work to eliminate the waste, fraud, and abuse currently found within the federal government.<br /> </p>" /> Skip to Content Deficit Spending Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print this Page Share by Email America's $38 trillion national debt is increasing at over  $70,000 per second . While I recognize that the process of righting our national budget will come with growing pains, we must remember Thomas Jefferson's warning that "public debt [is] the greatest of the dangers to be feared." If we wish to survive as a nation and preserve the Republic for our children and grandchildren, Congress must stop spending money we do not have and work to eliminate the waste, fraud, and abuse currently found within the federal government.
